literature.headline_zh: 沙粒病毒科本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期沙粒病毒科研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 该研究在豚鼠模型中证明了 CENis 对 拉沙热 和阿根廷出血热病毒感染的成功治疗效果,并鉴定了几种具有 抗病毒药物 活性的 CENis 对其他高致病性 沙粒病毒 的活性。 [10.1128/mbio.00880-26]
rVSV-MACV1 在细胞和病毒颗粒中表达的 MACV GPC 水平高于 rVSV-MACV5,但 rVSV-MACV5 引发了更高的总 IgG 和针对 MACV 的中和抗体。使用 rVSV-MACV5 初免和 rVSV-JUNV 加强的顺序免疫实现了最高水平的 MACV 和 JUNV 反应性抗体。 [10.1128/jvi.00357-26]

卡杜纳报告了 54 例疑似病例、8 例确诊病例,确诊病例中死亡 5 例(病死率 62.5%),其中包括 2 例医护人员感染。卡诺报告疑似病例7例,确诊病例2例,死亡2例。确诊病例中有 1 例死亡(病死率:50.0%,1/2),疑似病例中有 2 例死亡(病死率:28.6%,2/7)。卡杜纳的暴发被延长,而卡诺的暴发被迅速遏制。两个州都实现了完整的接触者追踪。 [10.37432/jieph-d-25-00240]
该研究显示,2019 年至 2024 年接受测试的儿童总体阳性率为 10.3%,其中年度阳性率在 2023 年(23.9%)和 2020 年(22.7%)达到峰值,并在 2021 年下降(13.6%)。年龄是一个强有力的预测因素:5-12 岁的儿童(AOR = 1.790,第 17 页)。 [10.11648/j.wjph.20261103.17]

literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: The study demonstrated successful therapeutic efficacy of CENis against Lassa fever and Argentine hemorrhagic fever virus infections in guinea pig models and identified several CENis with antiviral activity against other highly pathogenic arenaviruses. [10.1128/mbio.00880-26]

rVSV-MACV1 expressed higher MACV GPC levels in cells and virions than rVSV-MACV5, yet rVSV-MACV5 elicited higher total IgG and neutralizing antibodies against MACV. Sequential immunization with rVSV-MACV5 prime and rVSV-JUNV boost achieved the highest levels of MACV- and JUNV-reactive antibodies. [10.1128/jvi.00357-26]

Kaduna reported 54 suspected cases, 8 confirmed cases, and 5 deaths among confirmed cases (CFR 62.5%), including 2 healthcare worker infections. Kano reported 7 suspected cases, 2 confirmed cases, and 2 deaths. [10.37432/jieph-d-25-00240]

The study showed an overall positivity rate of 10.3% among children tested from 2019 to 2024, with notable annual positivity rates peaking in 2023 (23.9%) and 2020 (22.7%) and a decline in 2021 (13.6%). 该研究在豚鼠模型中证明了 CENis 对 拉沙热 和阿根廷出血热病毒感染的成功治疗效果,并鉴定了几种具有 抗病毒药物 活性的 CENis 对其他高致病性 沙粒病毒 的活性。 [10.1128/mbio.00880-26]。
rVSV-MACV1 在细胞和病毒颗粒中表达的 MACV GPC 水平高于 rVSV-MACV5,但 rVSV-MACV5 引发了更高的总 IgG 和针对 MACV 的中和抗体。使用 rVSV-MACV5 初免和 rVSV-JUNV 加强的顺序免疫实现了最高水平的 MACV 和 JUNV 反应性抗体。
卡杜纳报告了 54 例疑似病例、8 例确诊病例,确诊病例中死亡 5 例(病死率 62.5%),其中包括 2 例医护人员感染。卡诺报告疑似病例7例,确诊病例2例,死亡2例。确诊病例中有 1 例死亡(病死率:50.0%,1/2),疑似病例中有 2 例死亡(病死率:28.6%,2/7)。卡杜纳的暴发被延长,而卡诺的暴发被迅速遏制。两个州都实现了完整的接触者追踪。
该研究显示,2019 年至 2024 年接受测试的儿童总体阳性率为 10.3%,其中年度阳性率在 2023 年(23.9%)和 2020 年(22.7%)达到峰值,并在 2021 年下降(13.6%)。年龄是一个强有力的预测因素:5-12 岁的儿童(AOR = 1.790,第 17 页)。
brief_items_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.

The study demonstrated successful therapeutic efficacy of CENis against Lassa fever and Argentine hemorrhagic fever virus infections in guinea pig models and identified several CENis with antiviral activity against other highly pathogenic arenaviruses.
rVSV-MACV1 expressed higher MACV GPC levels in cells and virions than rVSV-MACV5, yet rVSV-MACV5 elicited higher total IgG and neutralizing antibodies against MACV.

Kaduna reported 54 suspected cases, 8 confirmed cases, and 5 deaths among confirmed cases (CFR 62.5%), including 2 healthcare worker infections. Kano reported 7 suspected cases, 2 confirmed cases, and 2 deaths.

The study showed an overall positivity rate of 10.3% among children tested from 2019 to 2024, with notable annual positivity rates peaking in 2023 (23.9%) and 2020 (22.7%) and a decline in 2021 (13.6%).

papers.title: Lassa fever and Argentine hemorrhagic fever treatment in guinea pigs using broad-spectrum cap-dependent endonuclease inhibitors
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The class Bunyaviricetes encompasses several highly pathogenic viruses that cause lethal hemorrhagic fevers. Due to their limited prevention and treatment options and high pathogenicity, these viruses require handling in biosafety level-4 facilities. Within the bunyaviruses, arenaviruses are particularly notable for their pathogenicity and ability to cause severe hemorrhagic disease in humans. The cap-dependent endonuclease (CEN) is a unique and crucial enzyme involved in the replication cycle of these viruses. As humans do not possess a similar enzyme, CEN represents an ideal target for antiviral drug development with reduced risk of side effects. Recently, we identified a promising CEN inhibitor (CENi) demonstrating potent inhibition of virus replication. In this manuscript, we demonstrate the successful therapeutic efficacy of CENis against Lassa fever and Argentine hemorrhagic fever virus infections in guinea pig models of lethal hemorrhagic fever. In addition, we identified several CENis with antiviral activity against other highly pathogenic arenaviruses. These findings further support the potential of CENis as therapeutic agents for arenavirus infections that cause severe and often lethal hemorrhagic fever. Collectively, our results suggest that CENis are promising candidates for pan-arenavirus therapy and may also have broader utility against other CEN-containing viruses for which no approved antiviral treatments currently exist. IMPORTANCE Arenaviruses, such as Lassa virus and Junin virus, cause severe hemorrhagic fevers in humans and are associated with high mortality rates and limited treatment options. Because of their pathogenicity and potential for outbreaks, these viruses represent an important global health threat. The viral cap-dependent endonuclease (CEN) plays a critical role in arenavirus replication by enabling the cap-snatching process required for viral mRNA synthesis. Notably, mammalian cells lack a comparable enzyme, making CEN an attractive target for antiviral drug development. In this study, we demonstrate that inhibitors targeting the arenavirus CEN effectively suppress viral replication and provide therapeutic protection in animal models of lethal Lassa virus and Junin virus infections. We also identify compounds with antiviral activity against multiple highly pathogenic arenaviruses. These findings establish CEN inhibition as a promising strategy for the development of broad-spectrum antivirals against arenaviruses that cause life-threatening hemorrhagic fevers.

papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Recombinant vesicular stomatitis virus (rVSV) is a powerful vaccine platform that elicits durable cellular and humoral immune responses. rVSV vaccines have successfully been used for various hemorrhagic fever-causing viruses. analysis.research_question_and_background: Machupo virus (MACV) causes Bolivian hemorrhagic fever with high mortality and no approved vaccines exist, creating a critical public-health need for effective countermeasures. The study addresses a knowledge gap on how genome position of the MACV glycoprotein complex (GPC) in recombinant vesicular stomatitis virus (rVSV) vectors influences immunogenicity.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study engineered rVSV vectors expressing MACV GPC in two genome positions and compared them to a related New World arenavirus, Junín virus (JUNV), using sequential immunization strategies. Vaccine candidates were evaluated for replication, antigen expression, and immune responses.
analysis.methods: rVSV-MACV1 and rVSV-MACV5 vectors were constructed with MACV GPC in the first or fifth genome position, respectively, and antigen expression was quantified in infected cells and virions. Humoral and cellular immune responses were measured after vaccination, and sequential immunization with rVSV-MACV5 prime followed by rVSV-JUNV boost was tested.
analysis.main_results: rVSV-MACV1 expressed higher MACV GPC levels in cells and virions than rVSV-MACV5, yet rVSV-MACV5 elicited higher total IgG and neutralizing antibodies against MACV. Sequential immunization with rVSV-MACV5 prime and rVSV-JUNV boost achieved the highest levels of MACV- and JUNV-reactive antibodies.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings indicate that higher antigen expression does not necessarily correlate with stronger immune responses, and genome position in rVSV vectors can modulate immunogenicity. The study provides new evidence on sequential immunization strategies to broaden cross-reactive antibody responses against New World arenaviruses.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results inform rVSV vaccine design for MACV and related New World arenaviruses by identifying genome position effects on immunogenicity and supporting sequential immunization as a strategy to enhance cross-reactive antibody responses.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro antigen expression and immune response measurements in a controlled experimental setting, and its findings require validation in animal models and clinical trials to assess protective efficacy and safety.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated recombinant vesicular stomatitis virus (rVSV) vaccines expressing the Machupo virus (MACV) glycoprotein complex (GPC) in different genome positions to determine their impact on immunogenicity. The authors constructed rVSV-MACV1 and rVSV-MACV5 vectors with GPC in the first or fifth genome position, respectively, and measured antigen expression and immune responses. Although rVSV-MACV1 produced higher antigen levels, rVSV-MACV5 elicited stronger humoral responses, including neutralizing antibodies. Sequential immunization with rVSV-MACV5 prime followed by a Junín virus (JUNV) boost yielded the highest cross-reactive antibody levels. The findings highlight that genome position in rVSV vectors can modulate immunogenicity and suggest sequential immunization as a strategy to broaden protection against New World arenaviruses. The study provides a foundation for vaccine development but requires further validation in vivo and in clinical settings.

The study addresses a knowledge gap on how genome position of the MACV glycoprotein complex (GPC) in recombinant vesicular stomatitis virus (rVSV) vectors influences immunogenicity.
elements_en.study_design_and_population: The study engineered rVSV vectors expressing MACV GPC in two genome positions and compared them to a related New World arenavirus, Junín virus (JUNV), using sequential immunization strategies. Vaccine candidates were evaluated for replication, antigen expression, and immune responses.
elements_en.methods: rVSV-MACV1 and rVSV-MACV5 vectors were constructed with MACV GPC in the first or fifth genome position, respectively, and antigen expression was quantified in infected cells and virions. Humoral and cellular immune responses were measured after vaccination, and sequential immunization with rVSV-MACV5 prime followed by rVSV-JUNV boost was tested.
elements_en.main_results: rVSV-MACV1 expressed higher MACV GPC levels in cells and virions than rVSV-MACV5, yet rVSV-MACV5 elicited higher total IgG and neutralizing antibodies against MACV. Sequential immunization with rVSV-MACV5 prime and rVSV-JUNV boost achieved the highest levels of MACV- and JUNV-reactive antibodies.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings indicate that higher antigen expression does not necessarily correlate with stronger immune responses, and genome position in rVSV vectors can modulate immunogenicity. The study provides new evidence on sequential immunization strategies to broaden cross-reactive antibody responses against New World arenaviruses.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results inform rVSV vaccine design for MACV and related New World arenaviruses by identifying genome position effects on immunogenicity and supporting sequential immunization as a strategy to enhance cross-reactive antibody responses.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro antigen expression and immune response measurements in a controlled experimental setting, and its findings require validation in animal models and clinical trials to assess protective efficacy and safety.

papers.title_zh: 重组水泡性口炎病毒载体疫苗在不同基因组位置表达马丘波病毒糖蛋白的免疫原性
papers.source_body_en: ABSTRACT Recombinant vesicular stomatitis virus (rVSV) is a powerful vaccine platform that elicits durable cellular and humoral immune responses. rVSV vaccines have successfully been used for various hemorrhagic fever-causing viruses. Here, we create and evaluate rVSV vaccines for Machupo virus (MACV), a highly pathogenic New World (NW) mammarenavirus that causes Bolivian hemorrhagic fever. VSV genome rearrangements impact attenuation of the viral vector and the immune response to the vaccine. Therefore, in this study, we directly compare the effect of altering the MACV glycoprotein complex (GPC) position in the VSV genome on humoral and cellular immune responses to vaccination by evaluating replication, antigen expression, and immunogenicity of rVSVs expressing MACV GPC in the first position of the genome (rVSV-MACV1) and in the traditional glycoprotein gene position (rVSV-MACV5). rVSV-MACV1 expresses higher levels of MACV GPC in infected cells and in virions, but the increased antigen does not translate to a more robust immune response. rVSV-MACV5 elicits higher levels of total IgG and neutralizing antibodies than rVSV-MACV1, but similar levels of MACV-specific T cells. To further investigate vaccine strategies for MACV and other NW arenaviruses such as Junín virus (JUNV), we evaluated the humoral immune response to sequential immunization with rVSVs expressing MACV and JUNV GPCs. The highest levels of MACV and JUNV reactive antibodies were achieved using an rVSV-MACV5 prime followed by rVSV-JUNV boost. The data from our study have implications for rVSV vaccine design and provide a foundation for the development of rVSV-vectored vaccines for MACV and other NW arenaviruses. IMPORTANCE Machupo virus (MACV) is a highly pathogenic New World (NW) mammarenavirus that causes Bolivian hemorrhagic fever (BHF). Because of their high mortality rates, MACV and other NW arenaviruses represent a significant public health threat. However, no approved vaccines for MACV exist. Here, we describe recombinant vesicular stomatitis virus (rVSV) vaccines that express the MACV glycoprotein complex (GPC) in different positions of the VSV genome and characterize the humoral and cellular immune response to each. We also investigate sequential immunization with rVSVs expressing MACV GPC and a related NW arenaviral antigen, Junín virus GPC, in an effort to elicit broadly cross-reactive antibody responses. The conclusions from our study are twofold: data presented here provide further understanding of rVSV vaccine vectors and how genome rearrangements can be leveraged for vaccine development, and the results from our study may inform future vaccine development for MACV and other NW arenaviruses.

papers.title: Concurrent Lassa fever outbreaks in Kaduna and Kano States, Nigeria: Lessons in Health Worker Safety and Emergency Response
papers.abstract: Introduction: Lassa fever remains a major public health threat in Nigeria, with recurrent seasonal outbreaks causing significant morbidity and mortality. In 2025, concurrent outbreaks occurred in Kaduna and Kano States, prompting coordinated surveillance and emergency response efforts. This study documents the epidemiology of these outbreaks and highlights lessons in outbreak detection, healthcare worker safety, and response coordination. Methods: A retrospective descriptive study was conducted using surveillance, laboratory, and case management data from the NCDC-supported surveillance system in Kaduna State and the Kano State Centre for Disease Control (KNCDC), with technical support from the World Health Organization (WHO) in Kano State. Laboratory confirmation was performed using real-time reverse transcriptase polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR). Kaduna’s outbreak occurred from epidemiological weeks 1–28 (January–July 2025), while Kano’s outbreak occurred in epidemiological week 15 (April 2025). All suspected cases meeting the national case definition were included. Data sources included SORMAS, situation reports, laboratory records, and health facility data. Descriptive and comparative analyses were performed using Microsoft Excel 365. Results: Kaduna reported 54 suspected cases, 8 confirmed cases, and 5 deaths among confirmed cases (CFR 62.5%), including 2 healthcare worker infections. Kano reported 7 suspected cases, 2 confirmed cases, and 2 deaths. One death occurred among confirmed cases (CFR: 50.0%, 1/2), while the second occurred among a suspected case (CFR: 28.6%, 2/7). Using confirmed cases as the denominator, Kaduna had a higher CFR than Kano (62.5%, 5/8 vs. Kaduna’s outbreak was prolonged, while Kano’s outbreak was rapidly contained. Both states achieved complete contact tracing. Conclusion: Differences in outbreak outcomes highlight the importance of timely detection, strong infection prevention and control (IPC), healthcare worker protection, coordinated response and effective surveillance systems for preventing wider transmission.

Health Five States Account for 86% of Nigeria’s 1,000 Lassa Fever Cases BrandIconImage 2 days ago Helen Aremu Bauchi, Ondo, Taraba, Benue and Edo remain the country’s major hotspots as death toll rises to 237 Five states have accounted for 86 per cent of Nigeria’s 1,000 confirmed Lassa fever cases recorded so far in 2026, with Bauchi, Ondo, Taraba, Benue and Edo continuing to bear the heaviest burden of the disease. The latest figures from the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) show that Lassa fever has been reported across 23 states and 116 local government areas since the beginning of the year. According to the agency’s Lassa Fever Situation Report for epidemiological Week 30, covering July 20 to 26, Nigeria recorded 17 new confirmed infections during the week, pushing the cumulative number of cases to 1,000. The outbreak has also claimed 237 lives, translating to a case fatality rate of 23.7 per cent. Although the number of new infections recorded in Week 30 declined compared with the previous week, when 20 cases were confirmed, the overall disease burden continued to rise. The cumulative number of confirmed cases increased from 983 in Week 29 to 1,000 in Week 30, while the death toll rose from 231 to 237. The case fatality rate also edged upwards from 23.5 per cent to 23.7 per cent. Four states record fresh infections The NCDC report showed that the 17 new cases recorded during the latest reporting week came from four states — Ondo, Bauchi, Edo and Benue. The continued emergence of new infections in states that already account for a significant proportion of the national caseload highlights the persistent transmission of Lassa fever in some parts of the country. Bauchi, Ondo, Taraba, Benue and Edo have consistently featured among the states most affected by the disease, accounting collectively for the vast majority of confirmed infections recorded in 2026. The concentration of cases in the five states also underscores the uneven geographical distribution of Lassa fever in Nigeria and places increased pressure on health authorities in affected areas to maintain surveillance and strengthen early detection. For the states at the centre of the outbreak, sustained access to diagnostic services, effective case management and infection-prevention measures remains critical to limiting further transmission and reducing deaths. Young adults among most affected The latest epidemiological data also indicate that Lassa fever continues to affect a predominantly young adult population. People between the ages of 21 and 30 years were identified as the most affected age group, pointing to a significant burden among Nigerians in their economically active years. The pattern reinforces the need for continued public awareness and preventive measures, particularly in communities where the disease is endemic. Healthcare workers face occupational risk The outbreak is also posing a continuing threat to healthcare workers involved in the treatment of infected patients. The NCDC reported one new Lassa fever infection among healthcare workers during Week 30, compared with no new healthcare worker infection in the preceding week. The development highlights the occupational risks faced by doctors, nurses, laboratory personnel, caregivers and other health workers who may come into contact with patients whose infections have not yet been diagnosed. Because Lassa fever can be transmitted through contact with the blood and other body fluids of infected people, strict infection-prevention and control measures remain essential in healthcare settings. Early recognition and diagnosis are particularly important because patients may initially present with symptoms that resemble other common illnesses, potentially increasing the risk of delayed treatment and exposure among healthcare personnel. How Lassa fever spreads Lassa fever is an acute viral illness that is endemic in parts of West Africa, including Nigeria. The disease remains a recurring public-health challenge, particularly during periods when transmission increases in affected communities. The primary route of transmission to humans is through contact with food or household items contaminated by the urine or faeces of infected multimammate rats, which are the principal reservoir of the virus. Human-to-human transmission can also occur, particularly through direct contact with the blood or body fluids of infected individuals. This makes healthcare facilities a critical point for infection prevention, especially where patients present with symptoms that could be associated with Lassa fever. Surveillance remains critical With confirmed infections now reaching 1,000 in 2026, the latest figures highlight the importance of sustained surveillance across affected and neighbouring states. While the decline in weekly cases from 20 to 17 may offer some indication of a reduction in new infections during the reporting period, the rise in cumulative cases and deaths shows that the outbreak remains a significant public-health concern. Health authorities will therefore need to maintain vigilance, particularly in the five states responsible for the overwhelming share of reported infections, while strengthening early detection, laboratory confirmation, treatment, contact tracing and infection-prevention measures. The continued infection of healthcare workers also serves as a reminder that controlling Lassa fever requires not only community-level prevention but also robust protection for those on the frontline of the response. Health Five States Account for 86% of Nigeria’s 1,000 Lassa Fever Cases BrandIconImage 2 days ago Helen Aremu Bauchi, Ondo, Taraba, Benue and Edo remain the country’s major hotspots as death toll rises to 237 Five states have accounted for 86 per cent of Nigeria’s 1,000 confirmed Lassa fever cases recorded so far in 2026, with Bauchi, Ondo, Taraba, Benue and Edo continuing to bear the heaviest burden of the disease. The latest figures from the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) show that Lassa fever has been reported across 23 states and 116 local government areas since the beginning of the year. According to the agency’s Lassa Fever Situation Report for epidemiological Week 30, covering July 20 to 26, Nigeria recorded 17 new confirmed infections during the week, pushing the cumulative number of cases to 1,000. The outbreak has also claimed 237 lives, translating to a case fatality rate of 23.7 per cent. Although the number of new infections recorded in Week 30 declined compared with the previous week, when 20 cases were confirmed, the overall disease burden continued to rise. The cumulative number of confirmed cases increased from 983 in Week 29 to 1,000 in Week 30, while the death toll rose from 231 to 237. The case fatality rate also edged upwards from 23.5 per cent to 23.7 per cent. Four states record fresh infections The NCDC report showed that the 17 new cases recorded during the latest reporting week came from four states — Ondo, Bauchi, Edo and Benue. The continued emergence of new infections in states that already account for a significant proportion of the national caseload highlights the persistent transmission of Lassa fever in some parts of the country. Bauchi, Ondo, Taraba, Benue and Edo have consistently featured among the states most affected by the disease, accounting collectively for the vast majority of confirmed infections recorded in 2026. The concentration of cases in the five states also underscores the uneven geographical distribution of Lassa fever in Nigeria and places increased pressure on health authorities in affected areas to maintain surveillance and strengthen early detection. For the states at the centre of the outbreak, sustained access to diagnostic services, effective case management and infection-prevention measures remains critical to limiting further transmission and reducing deaths. Young adults among most affected The latest epidemiological data also indicate that Lassa fever continues to affect a predominantly young adult population. People between the ages of 21 and 30 years were identified as the most affected age group, pointing to a significant burden among Nigerians in their economically active years. The pattern reinforces the need for continued public awareness and preventive measures, particularly in communities where the disease is endemic. Healthcare workers face occupational risk The outbreak is also posing a continuing threat to healthcare workers involved in the treatment of infected patients. The NCDC reported one new Lassa fever infection among healthcare workers during Week 30, compared with no new healthcare worker infection in the preceding week. The development highlights the occupational risks faced by doctors, nurses, laboratory personnel, caregivers and other health workers who may come into contact with patients whose infections have not yet been diagnosed. Because Lassa fever can be transmitted through contact with the blood and other body fluids of infected people, strict infection-prevention and control measures remain essential in healthcare settings. Early recognition and diagnosis are particularly important because patients may initially present with symptoms that resemble other common illnesses, potentially increasing the risk of delayed treatment and exposure among healthcare personnel. How Lassa fever spreads Lassa fever is an acute viral illness that is endemic in parts of West Africa, including Nigeria. The disease remains a recurring public-health challenge, particularly during periods when transmission increases in affected communities. The primary route of transmission to humans is through contact with food or household items contaminated by the urine or faeces of infected multimammate rats, which are the principal reservoir of the virus. Human-to-human transmission can also occur, particularly through direct contact with the blood or body fluids of infected individuals. This makes healthcare facilities a critical point for infection prevention, especially where patients present with symptoms that could be associated with Lassa fever. Surveillance remains critical With confirmed infections now reaching 1,000 in 2026, the latest figures highlight the importance of sustained surveillance across affected and neighbouring states. While the decline in weekly cases from 20 to 17 may offer some indication of a reduction in new infections during the reporting period, the rise in cumulative cases and deaths shows that the outbreak remains a significant public-health concern. Health authorities will therefore need to maintain vigilance, particularly in the five states responsible for the overwhelming share of reported infections, while strengthening early detection, laboratory confirmation, treatment, contact tracing and infection-prevention measures. The continued infection of healthcare workers also serves as a reminder that controlling Lassa fever requires not only community-level prevention but also robust protection for those on the frontline of the response.
